chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari, from Abu Ya'qub al-Baghdadi, who said:

Ibn al-Sikkit said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Why did God send Moses son of Imran (peace be upon him) with the staff, the white hand, and means pertaining to magic; and sent Jesus with means pertaining to medicine; and sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and upon all the prophets with speech and eloquent discourse?'

So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'When God sent Moses (peace be upon him), magic was predominant among the people of his era. So he came to them from God with that which was beyond their power to produce anything like it, and by which he invalidated their magic and established the proof against them.'

And God sent Jesus (peace be upon him) at a time when chronic diseases had appeared and the people were in need of medicine. So he came to them from God with that which they had nothing comparable to — with which he revived the dead for them, cured those born blind and the lepers by God's permission, and established the proof against them.

And God sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) at a time when eloquent discourse and speech were predominant among the people of his era — and I believe he said: 'and poetry' — so he came to them from God, from His admonitions and His wisdom, with what invalidated their speech and established the proof against them.

He said: Then Ibn al-Sikkit said, 'By God, I have never seen anyone like you! So what is the proof upon mankind today?' He said: Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The intellect — by which the one who speaks truthfully on behalf of God is known and thus believed, and the one who lies on behalf of God is known and thus disbelieved.'
He said: Then Ibn al-Sikkit said, 'This, by God, is the answer!'

key_terms.آلَةُ السِّحْرِ: Means of magic — referring to Moses's miracles which outpaced the magic arts dominant in his time
key_terms.الزَّمَانَاتُ: Chronic diseases, long-term ailments — explaining why medical miracles were particularly apt for the era of Jesus
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: The truthful one — one who speaks genuinely on behalf of God
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Proof — a technical theological term (hujja) meaning the evidence or argument God establishes against His creation through prophets and Imams
key_terms.الْعَقْلُ: The Intellect ('aql) — in Shia theology, reason is a primary faculty through which divine guidance is recognized
key_terms.الْغَالِبُ: The predominant/dominant — what was most prevalent in each prophetic era, justifying the type of miracle sent
key_terms.الْكَاذِبُ: The liar — one who falsely claims to speak on behalf of God

ai.seo_question: Why did God send different miracles to Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith records a remarkable exchange between Ibn al-Sikkit, the celebrated Arab grammarian and companion of Imam al-Hadi (AS), and the Imam himself. Ibn al-Sikkit asked why each of the three great prophets — Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad — was sent with different miraculous gifts, and the Imam explained that God's signs were always suited to the dominant skill of each era: Moses faced master magicians, Jesus came to a people afflicted by illness, and Muhammad arose among masters of eloquent speech and poetry. When Ibn al-Sikkit then pressed the Imam on what the proof upon mankind is today (in their own era), the Imam replied with the defining answer: the intellect ('aql), which enables people to distinguish truth-tellers from liars. This teaching, from the chapter on 'Aql in al-Kafi, contextualizes divine proofs as adaptive to human capacity.
